summary: Adds an email search filter to the user index, plus new update and destroy endpoints. Also adds a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: The index action interpolates params[:q] directly into the SQL WHERE fragment. Any authenticated caller controls that text.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated caller can inject SQL and read or change any table, including api_token values.
findings.fix: Pass q as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Destroy action exempt from admin check
findings.problem: The change adds destroy to the except list of require_admin. The destroy action then deletes any user by id without an ownership check.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can delete every account, including admin accounts.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the except list so only admins can delete users.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback runs on both create and update. The new update endpoint therefore emails the user a welcome message on every edit.
findings.consequence: Existing users get repeated welcome emails whenever an admin edits them or any code saves the record.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the welcome email goes out once after the user is created.

findings.title: New endpoints and callback lack tests
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search filter, update, destroy or welcome email callback.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and query handling for these endpoints will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request tests for index search, update and destroy, including non-admin access cases.

dropped.reason: The require_admin filter guards update, and admins are meant to manage any user record.
